userSpecifiedSources:
Independent compilation of five U.S. government sources:

- NOAA/NWS SPC historical tornado database: https://www.spc.noaa.gov/wcm/#data
- NOAA NCEI Storm Events bulk tables: https://www.ncei.noaa.gov/pub/data/swdi/stormevents/csvfiles/
- NOAA/NWS Damage Assessment Toolkit: https://services.dat.noaa.gov/arcgis/rest/services/nws_damageassessmenttoolkit/DamageViewer/MapServer
- U.S. Census Bureau Population Estimates Program: https://www.census.gov/programs-surveys/popest.html
- U.S. Census Bureau 2020 Cartographic Boundary Files: https://www.census.gov/geographies/mapping-files/2020/geo/carto-boundary-file.html

NOAA snapshot collected September 14, 2026; Census snapshot collected September 15, 2026. Each source file retains its URL, retrieval time, and checksum in the archive. Population/housing estimates use vintage 2020 for 2010–2019 and vintage 2025 for 2020–2025; the county map is fixed at 2020.

Collection code, source notices, and release receipt: https://github.com/jakeryderv/us-tornado-data-2010-2025

This is a fixed 2010–2025 research snapshot with no scheduled refresh. Any deliberate corrections will be a separately versioned release.

resources.description: Start here: scope, source counts, limitations, and loading examples. The analysis tables are directly downloadable; full original sources are inside release.zip.bin.
Platform-neutral dataset card covering scope, units of observation, fields, transformations, missingness, EF-rating limitations, and source attribution.
Original NOAA/NWS and Census source links, reuse notices, third-party exceptions, and citation guidance. Government records are distinct from MIT-licensed project code.
Detailed collection rules, directory layout, field interpretation, verification methods, and geographic/time-coverage limitations for the five-source collection.
Machine-readable citation metadata for the frozen release: title, author, version, release date, and code repository.
MIT license for project code and original documentation. This does not relicense government records; see DATA_SOURCES.md for source reuse terms.
Machine-readable schema inventory: complete CSV headers, saved DAT layer field definitions, and typed analysis tables. Describes files inside the extracted release archive.
Release v1.2.0 inventory with source snapshot dates, code commit, sizes, and SHA-256 hashes for all 2,876 shared payload files. Paths are relative to the extracted archive root.
SHA-256 checksums for the shared payload and release_manifest.json. Use these after extraction; the outer transport archive hash is recorded separately in the GitHub release receipt.

Complete v1.2.0 dataset: 2,876 shared files (493 MB), packaged as a 292 MB ZIP with an extra .bin suffix to preserve original source archives. Includes all five source collections, nine consolidated Parquet/GeoParquet tables, annual summary, provenance, schemas, and checksums. The analysis tables are also downloadable separately. No cross-source event match or model split is supplied.
Field dictionary, transformations, units, nullable types, annual aggregation rules, rebuild instructions, and EF-classification limitations for the compact analysis layer.

20,164 retained SPC tornado tracks, 2010–2025. Descriptive field names, string identifiers, nullable EF ratings, explicit units, and coordinate plausibility flags. Unknown EF labels remain null; no cross-source joins or model split.
